header.name: Governing AI: Policy, History, Theory
header.description: In conceptualising Artificial Intelligence (Henceforth AI) as a social science category, this course will enable students to analyze the emerging field of AI regulation and governance, help them learn about the regulatory landscape of the AI, and equip them situate the regulatory landscape historically and theoretically. The course is divided in four parts. The first part introduces the central conceptual scheme built around the definitions of AI, and the concepts of regulation and governance. Part two surveys the AI regulateroy landscape globally and equips students analyze them through historical and conceptual devices outlined in the earlier parts.Part three traces the history of the blurring lines between humans and machines in terms of intellectual labour. The final part introduces the relevant literature drawn from political philosophy and theory to contextualise the idea of human political agency and the implications that blurred lines between machines and humans may have on it.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students would be able to conceptually define Artifically Intelligence

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students would be able to define governance in the context of AI.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will know the global regulatory landscape of AI governance.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to relate the computational aspects of AI with the larger socio-economic and political processes.

lecture_topics: Introduction: What is AI? aka, AI as a theoretical entity.
What does it mean to govern AI?
AI Regulation in the United States
When the lines get blurred: a. The moral economy of calculation.
b. Mind and machine as behavioural system.
c. From judgment to calculation, to intelligence.
The AI that governs? Or the AI that is governable?
